name: Renato Cesarini
scopeNote: Manager profile of Renato Cesarini across two counted spells: River Plate (1939 to 1944, partial dates: the day of appointment and departure were not found; the coach of 'La Máquina' in 1941 and 1942 Primera División titles, with Carlos Peucelle as co-coach in 1941) and Juventus (1959 to 1960, partial dates: Serie A 1959/60 per Spanish Wikipedia; English Wikipedia's infobox gives 1946 to 1948 instead, so the dates are in conflict). The River Plate spell is the subject of this profile. Excluded: Racing (1945), Banfield (1949), Boca Juniors (1950), Pordenone (1958 to 1959), Pumas UNAM (1964 to 1965), River Plate return (1965 to 1966), Argentina national team (1967 to 1968) and Huracán (1968), none of which had titles or tactical facts in the pages read. All spell dates here are years only (partial), because the sources give no days. Style: the evidence on the 1941 side is retrospective: Adolfo Pedernera moved from the left wing to a 'more central and withdrawn role' (en.wiki, 'La Máquina', 'one of the first uses of the figure of the false nine'). No period quote from Cesarini on his tactics was found, and no primary source on his coaching style was read.

sources.title: La Máquina - Wikipedia
sources.evidence: Page reader summary: in 1941 Cesarini and Peucelle, as coaches, 'started using the left winger Adolfo Pedernera as a man of reference', switching him to 'a more central and withdrawn role' and 'inviting him to alternate between driving into the box to finish moves off and sitting back to direct them'; 'It was one of the first uses of the figure of the false nine.' Retrospective, no period quote.
